sources.citation: Coe, Michael D., Javier Urcid, and Rex Koontz. 2019. Mexico: From the Olmecs to the Aztecs. 8th ed. London: Thames & Hudson. ISBN 978-0-500-84178-5.
sources.notes: Current Thames & Hudson handbook survey from Olmec through Aztec. Secondary; cross-check site facts against excavation reports.

sources.citation: Stirling, Matthew W. 1955. Stone Monuments of the Rio Chiquito, Veracruz, Mexico. Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 157. Washington, DC: Smithsonian Institution / GPO.
sources.notes: Primary BAE bulletin on Rio Chiquito / San Lorenzo-area stone monuments from Smithsonian–National Geographic work. Historical recording standards.

sources.citation: Bernal, Ignacio. 1969. The Olmec World. Translated by Doris Heyden and Fernando Horcasitas. Berkeley: University of California Press.
sources.notes: Classic secondary synthesis of Olmec archaeology and art (English translation of El mundo olmeca). Prefer site reports for excavation facts.

sources.citation: Grove, David C. Additional Chalcatzingo reporting and reinterpretation papers beyond Grove 1987 monograph already registered (monument programs; highland–Gulf interaction).
sources.notes: Additional primary/peer reporting on Chalcatzingo monuments and context. Complements src-olmec-grove-chalcatzingo-1987.

sources.citation: Cyphers, Ann. Reports/briefs on El Azuzul twin-figure monument group and related San Lorenzo hinterland sculpture contexts.
sources.notes: Primary Cyphers reporting on El Azuzul sculpture group. Prefer published descriptions; no forged monument photos.

sources.citation: Pool, Christopher A. Additional Tres Zapotes excavation/analysis publications deepening Pool 2003 / C14 sources already registered (Formative sequence; epi-Olmec transition).
sources.notes: Additional primary Tres Zapotes reporting. Epi-Olmec script/political labels remain interpretive.

sources.citation: Blomster, Jeffrey P., et al. Papers on Etlatongo (Mixteca Alta) Formative deposits and Olmec-style pottery exchange debates (complements Blomster–Neff–Glascock 2005 already registered).
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed highland Formative / Olmec-style pottery studies. Exchange directionality remains debated — keep unidirectional "mother culture" export models as hypothesis.

sources.citation: Diehl, Richard A. Additional Diehl syntheses on Olmec archaeology beyond Diehl 2004 already registered (museum/catalog essays; regional overviews).
sources.notes: Secondary Diehl overview materials. Prefer Coe–Diehl 1980 and site reports for excavation facts.

sources.citation: Taube, Karl A. Additional Olmec iconography studies beyond Taube 2004 Dumbarton Oaks volume already registered (maize god; rain symbolism).
sources.notes: Secondary iconographic analyses. Symbol readings are interpretive; do not treat as proven theology.

sources.citation: Clark, John E., and David Cheetham. Papers on Early Formative Soconusco / Gulf interaction and Olmec-style material distributions.
sources.notes: Secondary/peer interaction papers. Complements Clark & Pye 2000; interaction ≠ single mother-culture verdict.
